02A.desc: Whole or ground poultry, poultry parts, all foods containing poultry, poultry stuffing and poultry stuffing containing meat not heated so that all parts reached 165 °F (73.9 °C) or above for at least 15 seconds with no interruption of the cooking process in that approximately 8 pounds of cooked chicken wings was not heated to 165 °F as observed. Said food was observed with the inner portion of the food appearing pink and partially raw at the time of the inspection. Food observed inside a metal container in the 2-door lowboy refrigerator for 2 hours in the rear kitchen area as per FPC holder, William McCarthy. Said chicken wing was par-cooked, placed directly in the walk-in refrigerator for 10 hours, removed and placed directly in the 1-door reach-in refrigerator for 2 hours prior to testing as per FPC holder, William McCarthy. Corrective action: Food was rendered inedible and discarded by food worker. NYCHC 81.09(c)(1)

02B.desc: Time/Temperature Control for Safety hot food not held at or above 140 °F (60 °C), except during necessary preparation, in that two plate(s) of chicken wings (approximately 5 each) registered at 86 °F on the table adjacent to deep fryers in the kitchen. Time as a Public Health Control was not observed being used with said food(s). Food has been on the table for one hour, as per FPC holder's statement. Said food was cooked and then placed directly on the table where it was held prior to testing. Corrective action: Food was reheated to 165°F(73.9°C) within two hours and then cooling procedures were implemented by placing said food into a two-door lowboy refrigerator in the kitchen. NYCHC 81.09(a) Please Note: The Health Code describes the situations when food may be out of temperature. The OATH Appeals Unit has further clarified the rules. For example, food under "necessary preparation" may be out of temperature only when the preparation process requires food to be out of temperature. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit Oct. 4, 2012) (rejecting necessary preparation defense when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be out of temperature). And, food being reheated, thawed, cooled or labeled for time and temperature and monitored under Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) may be out of temperature only if the restaurant is following the required Health Code methods for these procedures. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit Feb. 12, 2014) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); DOHMH v. Gus & Steve Luncheonette, Inc., Dkt No. 2457312F1 (App. Unit Feb. 4, 2013) (same, thawing); DOHMH v. Palate Restaurant LLC, Dkt 09264-15F1 (App. Unit Oct. 19, 2015) (same, cooling); DOHMH v. LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit April 10, 2014) (same, TPHC). These rulings are available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

02G.desc: Time/Temperature Control for Safety cold food, other than processed fish, not held at or below 41 °F (5 °C) in that two whole brined raw pork butts (approximately 5 pounds each) in a tightly covered metal container registered at 46 °F inside the adequately-functioning walk-in refrigerator in the basement. Food has been at the observed location for 2 hours and 30 minutes, as per Kitchen Manager Bill McGovern's statement. Said food was placed in a brine inside the adequately-functioning walk-in refrigerator 1 day prior and left inside said walk-in refrigerator overnight. Said food was then removed from said walk-in refrigerator 2 hours and 30 minutes prior, removed from said brine, and direclty returned to said walk-in refrigerator, as per Kitchen Manager's statement. Said food was observed to be tightly covered, inhibiting proper cold holding. Corrective action: Food was rendered inedible and discarded by food worker. NYCHC 81.09(a) Note: NYCHC and OATH Law sets situations when food may be out of temperature (OOT). See, e.g., Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit 10/4/12) (rejecting necessary preparation when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be OOT); Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit 2/12/14) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); Gus & Steve Luncheonette, Inc., Dkt No. 2457312F1 (App. Unit 2/4/13) (same, thawing); Palate Restaurant LLC, Dkt 09264-15F1 (App. Unit 10/19/15) (same, cooling); LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit 4/10/14) (same, TPHC). Rulings available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

BICA72.desc: Respondent, EASTSIDE BULK LLC, is a regulated company, a broker registrant with the Commission.  On or about July 10, 2025, the Commission issued a directive to Respondent, requiring all broker registrants to submit a sample contract and a copy of the rate schedule provided to customers in New York City to ensure compliance with applicable Commission rules and regulations, or a notarized letter stating that the request was not applicable, due on or before July 24, 2025. The Directive specified that failure to respond constituted a violation of Commission rules. Respondent is in violation of 17 RCNY 1-09(d) and 6-04(b) for failing to answer the Commission directive requiring Respondent to submit a sample contract and a copy of the rate schedule provided to customers in New York City.

BICB58.desc: On May 31, 2025, at approximately 9:15 am, in front of 315 Norman Avenue, Brooklyn, NY, the undersigned Commission Investigator observed a green 2015 Western-Star dump truck with New York DMV license plate number 43245PF, BIC plate number L10334, and vehicle identification number 5KKMBEDVXFPGU3049. The vehicle is registered to Respondent MRT BWR Corp, a regulated company with the Commission. At the time of the observation, the vehicle was being operated by vehicle operator Enrico Conter.  Upon inspection, the vehicle observed had a roll-off container that was observed moving vertically at the rear of the container and causing a loud banging noise. A vehicle stop was conducted. Upon further inspection of the vehicle, the rear of the container was not secured to the vehicle chassis with a tiedown, hook or other equivalent mechanism as required by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations. As a result of not properly securing the rear of the container being transported, Respondent caused unnecessary and avoidable noise while operating the vehicle in violation of Commission rules and regulations.  Additionally, Respondents failure to comply with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulation, CFR Title 49 Part 393.143 (b) (3), requiring the rear of the container secured to the vehicle chassis to prevent lateral and vertical movement, violated Commission rules and regulations, 17 RCNY 7-02, requiring registrants to comply with all local, State, and Federal laws, rules, and regulations of governmental authorities that have jurisdiction over any of the registrants' activities, including, but not limited to, the transportation of trade waste in a safe manner.

The vehicle is registered to Respondent, J BASS & SON INC. The undersigned further observed J BASS & SON stenciled to the front doors of the vehicle. Upon investigation, the vehicle operator was identified as Ulises Prado.  The vehicle operator stated that the trade waste observed is from a job site at 87 Greene Street Manhattan New York. And was removing the waste to a transfer station. Upon a search of BIC records the above vehicle was not disclosed or assigned BIC plates prior to its operation. Thus, the Respondent permitted a vehicle to be used in the course of collecting, removing, or disposing of waste that has not been identified and covered by the registration and for which a fee has not been paid in violation of Commission rules and regulations.

BICB63.desc: On May 7th, 2025, at approximately 12:45pm, in front of 520 Kingsland Avenue, Brooklyn, NY, the undersigned Commission Investigator observed a 2019 Peterbilt dump truck with New Jersey DMV license plate number AU856S, BIC plate number R08350, and vehicle identification number 1NPXX4TX4KD602530. The vehicle is registered to the Respondent, Jaym Trans LLC., a regulated company with the Commission. At the time of observation, the vehicle was being operated by vehicle operator Fred R Albuja.  Stenciled on both of the vehicle cab doors was "JAYM, TRANS LLC" and no stenciling on the vehicle body. Respondent failed to stencil or imprint the company full business address with street address, city, and state on the vehicle body or upon the vehicle cab doors, at all times, as required by Commission rules and regulations.

BICB69.desc: On September 24, 2025, at approximately 8:22 am, in front of 451 Spencer Street Staten Island, NY, the undersigned Commission Investigator conducted a vehicle inspection on a red Ford dump truck bearing New Jersey State DMV plate number XNKD57 and vehicle identification number 1FDXF46S73ED01638. No BIC plates were observed affixed to this vehicle. The vehicle is registered to the respondent Elite Constructors Corp. At the time of this inspection the vehicle operator was identified as Hassan Jhangir. A BIC records check was performed on 09/24/2025 and it revealed that the driver and vehicle were disclosed to the Commission under BIC file # 514330. The check also showed that a set of BIC plates R12692 was assigned to this vehicle on 01/03/2025 but was never picked up by the respondent and affixed to the vehicle as required. The inspection also found that the vehicle operator could not locate inside the vehicle both the six-month inspection and certification of repair report and daily inspection reports and was unable to provide a copy of the reports to the Investigator for inspection, which is in violation of the Commission rules and regulations.

BICB72.desc: On September 23, 2024, at approximately 9:45 am, at 548 Varick Avenue, Brooklyn, NY, the undersigned observed a white 2019 Chevr Pickup truck with New York DMV plate 95792MM, BIC plate R10733 and VIN number 1HTKJPVKXKH862805. The vehicle is registered to Respondent, Pedrol Contracting Inc., a regulated company with the Commission. The vehicle operator was identified as Witt Wojciech, Janusz.  Upon request, the vehicle operator, Witt Wojciech, Janusz stated that he was unable to locate the daily vehicle inspection report from inside the vehicle and he was unable to produce the document upon request as required by Commission rules and regulations.

BICBK5.desc: On May 20, 2026, at approximately 5:44 pm, in front of 400 East 66th Street New York, NY, the undersigned Commission Investigator conducted vehicle inspection on a white / red 2012 Mack dump truck bearing New York State DMV plate number 35352NG, BIC plate number L13587 and vehicle identification number 1M2AU02C8CM006461. This vehicle is registered to the respondent J & N Dolcinium Inc, a regulated company with the Commission. At the time of the inspection, the vehicle operator was identified as Ljubisa Sosic. The vehicle inspection found that the respondent J & N Dolcinium Inc failed to have a NYS 25th Sires Highway Use Tax (HUT) Permit / sticker affixed to the vehicle, a violation under the NYS Tax Law Section 1815 Subsection A1. Respondent's failure to abide by Section 1815 Subsection A1 is in violation of Commission rules that require respondents to comply with all the laws, rules and regulations of Federal, State and local governmental authorities having jurisdiction over respondents' activities, including, but not limited to, NYS Dept of Taxation and Finance. The inspection also found that upon request by this Investigator the vehicle operator could not locate the six-month inspection and certification of repair report and was unbaled to provide copy of the report for review.
